title: Tenant QoS Batching API proto (brain dump)
content:
Context:
Small brain-dump for a tenant-aware batching layer that surfaces per-tenant QoS and cost/priority hints to the serving runtime. Goal is to let tenant teams express soft/hard latency objectives and batching preferences without changing client call shapes. Primary consumer: Dedicated and Private customers with mixed workloads and multiple SLAs per tenant (e.g., interactive UI vs background embedding flushes).

High-level goals:
- Allow per-tenant per-route QoS policies (latency SLO, max batch delay, priority weight).
- Keep client API unchanged (POST /v1/generate). Router/batcher should act as a transparent sidecar.
- Support runtime preemption and hedging when SLO risk is detected.
- Pricing signal: prefer batching when cost-sensitive.

Quick ascii diagram:

client -> ingress-router -> tenant-qos-batcher -> runtime-pool
                           |                      /-- model-variant A
                           |-> metrics & policy-store -|
                                                  \-- model-variant B

Behavior overview:
- Ingress-router tags each request with tenant_id, route_id, client_hint (interactive|bulk), and optional priority token.
- Tenant QoS Batcher consults policy-store cache (TTL 30s). Policy includes max_wait_ms, min_batch_size, priority_weight, cost_preference (economic|balanced|latency), fallback_policy.
- Batcher batches across routes only if policy allows routing-aggregation=true and no conflicting isolation constraints.
- When batch is formed, batch metadata includes 'priority_score' computed from tenant priority_weight * 1/(estimated_wait+1) + cost_discount.
- Runtime uses priority_score to order batch execution and to decide preemption when load is high.

Example policy (JSON blob stored in policy-store):
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "route": "/v1/generate/chat",
  "max_wait_ms": "50",
  "min_batch_size": "4",
  "priority_weight": "1.8",
  "cost_preference": "balanced",
  "routing-aggregation": "true",
  "fallback_policy": "fallback-to-smaller-model"
}

API surface (router <-> batcher):
POST /internal/batcher/enqueue
headers: X-Tenant-Id, X-Route-Id, X-Client-Hint, X-Priority-Token?
body: { request_id, input, token_budget_hint, client_timeout_ms }
response: { enqueue_id, estimated_dispatch_ms }

Dispatch event from batcher -> runtime:
POST /internal/runtime/dispatch
body: { batch_id, requests: [{enqueue_id, input_hash, token_budget_hint}], batch_meta: {priority_score, tenant_summary, aggregated_tokens} }

Runtime contract (notes):
- Runtime should treat batch_meta.priority_score as a soft signal. Decision to preempt or reorder is local but must emit telemetry when it violates a request's max_wait_ms.
- Support an immediate eviction hook: /internal/runtime/preempt/{batch_id} for urgent interactive requests.

Admission / pricing integration:
- Batcher monitors token_budget_hint vs observed tokens and can decide to defer non-critical batches if token burn threatens reserved capacity for high-priority tenants.
- Expose per-tenant 'cost-slack' metric to billing/alerts.

Repro examples (sequence):
1) UI request arrives for tenant X (interactive, max_wait_ms=25) -> enqueue -> batcher sees small batch forming -> if min_batch_size not met and waiting would exceed max_wait_ms, flush early and mark cost-penalty=true
2) Background embedding flush arrives (bulk, max_wait_ms=2000) -> batcher aggregates aggressively to reach quantization-friendly batch sizes

Open questions / TODOs:
- Policy resolution precedence: tenant-level vs route-level vs account-level. Proposed: route-level overrides tenant-level.
- How to surface quantitative SLO misses to customer? Slack alerts vs per-request header in response?
- Memory accounting for aggregated KV-caches when batching across model-variants. Need SLO for evictions.
- Security: ensure tenant isolation when routing-aggregation=true (no cross-tenant mixing). That should be a hard requirement.

Telemetry to emit:
- enqueue_latency, batch_formation_time, estimated_vs_actual_wait, cost_penalty_flag, priority_score_histogram, preemption_count

Implementation notes and quick plan:
- MVP: batcher as an ingress sidecar written in Go, local policy cache, REST wires. Start with policy fields: max_wait_ms, min_batch_size, priority_weight, cost_pref, fallback_policy.
- Phase 2: add ML-based batch formation estimator (predict token length distribution) and integrate with Optimize suggestion engine.

Slack snippets / links (for copy-paste):
- "INF-1293 has rough policy schema, iterating on priority_score calc - @evan please sanity check weighting + cost factor"
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/58 (proto sketches)

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep batcher response quick; don't block client threads on policy-store fetch (use stale cached policy).
- Make cost_preference default to 'balanced'.
- Add an end-to-end test sim: 80% interactive 20% bulk across 3 tenants, measure p50/p95 latency and token-cost delta.

Next steps:
- Draft real proto for enqueue/dispatch -> pair with Evan for wire compatibility test.
- Add small Perf harness to simulate (local harness in runtime repo).
- Bring to eng-brown-bag for feedback and compliance check.

-- end of dump --
